title: Chapter 4 Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of image tagging, pushing to registries, layers, saving/loading, and cleanup!

questions.question: What is the default registry if you don’t specify one in an image name?
questions.explanation: If no registry is provided, Docker defaults to `docker.io`, which is Docker Hub.

questions.question: What does the `latest` tag guarantee?
options: It is always the most recent version of the image
It is the most stable version
It is the default tag when none is specified
It is the smallest image size
questions.explanation: `latest` is simply the default tag. It does not imply any special status like newest or most stable.

questions.question: `docker tag` creates a copy of the image with a new name, doubling disk usage.
questions.explanation: Tagging just creates a new reference to the same image ID; no extra disk space is used.

questions.question: To push an image to your personal Docker Hub account, you must tag it as `_______/myrepo:mytag`.
questions.explanation: You can only push to repositories under your own Docker Hub username (namespace).

questions.question: What command authenticates your Docker client with a registry?
questions.explanation: `docker login` stores your credentials for pushing/pulling private images.

questions.question: Why would `docker push alpine:latest` fail for a normal user?
questions.explanation: The official `alpine` image lives in the `library` namespace, which only Docker maintainers can push to.

questions.question: What information does `docker history` provide?
options: A list of all containers that used the image
The commands (layers) used to build the image and their sizes
The network traffic of the image
The Docker version used to build the image
questions.explanation: `docker history` shows each layer’s creation command, size, and time.

questions.question: If two images both use `alpine:3.18` as a base, the alpine layers are stored twice on disk.
questions.explanation: Docker shares layers by their content hash. Identical layers are stored only once.

questions.question: Which command exports an image to a tar file?
questions.explanation: `docker save` exports images preserving layers. `docker export` works on containers and flattens them.

questions.question: What command loads an image from a tar file into Docker?
questions.explanation: `docker load` reads a tar stream (from `docker save`) and loads the image.

questions.question: How can you transfer an image directly to a remote Docker host over SSH without an intermediate file?
options: docker save myimage | ssh host 'docker load'
questions.explanation: Piping `docker save` to `ssh` is a clever one‑liner to move images across machines.

questions.question: What does `docker image prune` remove by default?
questions.explanation: Without `-a`, `prune` only removes dangling images — those not tagged and not referenced by any container.

questions.question: `docker image prune -a` deletes all images not currently used by any container.
questions.explanation: The `-a` flag expands the prune scope to all unused images, even tagged ones, as long as no container references them.

questions.question: Which command shows disk usage of Docker objects?
questions.explanation: `docker system df` gives a summary of disk usage by images, containers, volumes, and build cache.

questions.question: What is the effect of `docker system prune -a --volumes`?
options: Removes all Docker data, including running containers
Removes stopped containers, unused networks, dangling & unused images, build cache, and unused volumes
questions.explanation: This aggressive command cleans up everything that isn’t being used by running containers, including volumes.

questions.question: To search Docker Hub for images containing the word 'mysql', use `docker _____ mysql`.
questions.explanation: `docker search` queries Docker Hub for public images matching the search term.

questions.question: In the image reference `registry.example.com:5000/team/app:v2`, what is the registry?
questions.explanation: The registry includes the host and port. Here it’s `registry.example.com:5000`.

questions.question: You can push an image to Docker Hub without logging in if the repository is public.
questions.explanation: You must authenticate to push, regardless of the repository’s visibility.

questions.question: What is the main advantage of the layered image architecture?
options: It makes images smaller by compressing each layer individually
Layers are shared across images, saving disk and transfer time
It allows multiple containers to write to the same layer
It improves network speed by using multicast
questions.explanation: Layer sharing is the key — identical base layers are stored once and reused, reducing pull and storage overhead.

questions.question: What does the `--filter "until=24h"` option do in `docker image prune`?
options: Removes images created within the last 24 hours
Removes all images except those created in the last 24 hours
Prunes containers that have been stopped for 24 hours
questions.explanation: The `until` filter targets images created before the given duration (or timestamp). So `24h` means older than 24 hours.
